candidates.name: Coordinate transformations
verified_facts: GNSS positioning in Great Britain is based on ETRS89 while OS mapping uses OSGB36 British National Grid.
OS states a coordinate transformation is required between those systems.
OSTN15 links positions to OSGB36 British National Grid while OSGM15 links GNSS heights to mean-sea-level based height datums such as ODN.
semantic_limits: Horizontal coordinate transformation and vertical datum transformation are separate error-budget components and must not be collapsed into one assumed accuracy value.

candidates.name: OS Net & GNSS questions and answers
verified_facts: OS warns precise GNSS heights are more difficult than horizontal coordinates and antenna phase-centre handling matters.

OS states about 2cm height accuracy at one standard error can be achieved with four hours of continuous GNSS observations at a primary survey station; shorter observations are generally less accurate.
OSGM15 accuracy is about 8mm rms for mainland Britain, with relative model error over a 10km extent only a few millimetres.
semantic_limits: OSGM15 model accuracy is not the total GNSS or LiDAR height uncertainty; observation, sensor, survey and raster errors remain separate.
